newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. reports progress in military talks on Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: U.N. reports progress in military talks on Cyprus.

text.p: An indirect military dialogue between the two rival sides on the divided island of Cyprus has made some progress, an official for the United Nations force deployed on the island said on Friday.
"After months of discussing the package with both sides we have made certain progress and things look more promising," U.N. spokesman Waldemar Rokoszewski told Reuters.
The English-lanugage daily Cyprus Mail reported on Friday that a "breakthrough" had been achieved in the talks, quoting U.N. sources.

U.N. officials have declined to state in which area progress has been made, citing the confidential nature of the military talks, held indirectly between Greek and Turkish Cypriots with the U.N. acting as the go-between.

The United Nations wants the two sides to agree on a package relating to unmanning sentry posts among troops on either side of the 180 km (110 mile) ceasefire line which has split the two communities for two decades, and unloading weapons. It also imposes a code of conduct for soldiers to follow.
The United Nations intensified efforts for the proposals to be accepted by the two sides after violent ceasefire line incidents last summer which claimed the lives of two Greek Cypriots.
"We have not achieved our goal, we are far from there but there are some indications that we may make progress," said Rokoszewski.

The United Nations have for years been trying to broker a political settlement to reunite the island, partitioned after Turkey invaded its north in 1974 in the wake of a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time.
Turkey has some 30,000 troops deployed in northern Cyprus, declared a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in 1983 recognised only by Ankara.
